summary.headline: Ester Industries Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA of INR53.6 crore (15.5% margin) excluding INR10.24 crore FX-loan MTM; reported net loss of INR27.5 crore for FY26.
summary.overview: Management framed Q4 FY26 as an inflection point, citing moderation of Chinese dumping and US tariff disruption plus higher BOPET prices and a weaker rupee lifting spreads. Consolidated total income rose 7.2% YoY to INR345.1 crore in Q4, with reported EBITDA of INR43.3 crore (12.6%) and PAT of INR7.9 crore. Full-year consolidated net loss of INR27.5 crore was driven mainly by non-cash MTM losses on euro-denominated term loans and a INR2.7 crore labour-code gratuity charge. Management expects BOPET margins to hold for 18 to 24 months, though Specialty Polymers softened in the quarter on demand loss in one marquee product and mix shift.

segments.name: Polyester Films (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 films revenue INR321 crore (+14.9% YoY) on 19,656 MT volume (+2.3% YoY); FY26 volume 80,517 MT (+5.1%). VAS products were 25% of FY26 volume, growing 14.5% in volume despite US tariff-related loss.

segments.name: Specialty Polymers
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR179.3 crore (+16% from INR155.2 crore) on 3,836 MT (+21%); segment EBIT INR58.7 crore at 32.7% margin. Q4 volume was 658 MT and revenue INR22.62 crore, with lower demand for one marquee product and mix shift toward lower-margin VAP products.

segments.name: Chips
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew about 2.2x YoY to INR65.7 crore on higher third-party volumes. Q4 segment EBIT INR42 crore (+73% YoY), margin 13% (+440 bps).

segments.name: rPET
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 5,325 MT (+258%), revenue INR59.3 crore (3.7x from INR16.2 crore). Q4 volume 1,677 MT (+126% YoY). A 20,000 MT per annum rPET extruder was commissioned in Hyderabad.

segments.name: Ester Filmtech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 sales volume 9,886 MT (+53.3%), utilisation 85% vs 59%. Reported EBITDA INR18.6 crore (14.1%); adjusted INR24.6 crore (18.7%). FY26 total income INR455.4 crore (+29.3%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects meaningful BOPET margin improvement in FY27 and beyond; sustained BOPET margins projected for about 18 to 24 months.
Q1 FY27 12-micron VA spread expected at INR30 to INR35/kg, versus INR32 to INR33 in Q4 FY26.
FY27 capex about INR70 crore consolidated: INR15 crore for new projects (stated IRR above 20%) and the balance for sustenance and maintenance; FY27 repayments about INR85 crore.
Borrowings targeted below INR40 crore by 31 March 2027, implying significant net debt reduction; cost of funds 9-10% consolidated.

ELITe (textile-to-textile chemical recycling JV) expected operational around end-CY28 (management also said commencement by Q4 CY28 / Q1 CY29); no P&L impact in FY27. First phase of about 70,000 tonnes targets close to USD150 million revenue at full utilisation with 40-45% EBITDA margin.

Management targets Specialty Polymers revenue of about INR200 crore in FY27 (not formally committed) and 20% growth annually; targets VAS share of films to 60%+ and Specialty Polymers share of about 20-25% in 2-3 years.
Expected ROCE above 20% over the next 8 to 10 quarters; historical ROCE about 32% (FY21) and 28% (FY20).
capex_capacity: Consolidated FY27 capex about INR70 crore, with INR15 crore for new high-return projects and the rest for sustenance and maintenance across both companies.
Existing assets could support about INR2,000-2,200 crore turnover at 100% utilisation, per management, with only sustenance capex needed before ELITe.
Ester Filmtech utilisation 85% in Q4 FY26; Ester Industries 72%; consolidated about 78%. Management says film lines could run at 100% but chooses balanced operation to avoid low-margin volume.
Hyderabad rPET extruder (20,000 MT per annum) commissioned to support PCR film demand and sale of film-grade and textile-grade rPET.

ELITe JV (50:50 with Ester Loop Infinite Technologies): FEED completed by Tata Consulting Engineers; Toyo Engineering appointed as engineering consultant; land acquisition in progress, expected in the next few months.
demand_pricing: Management says Indian BOPET industry operating rates are about 80%; demand growth expected at 8-10% p.a. versus 6-8% previously, supported by FMCG growth and PWMR-driven substitution from BOPP/BOPE.
Average 12-micron VA spread in Q4 FY26 was INR32-33/kg; management expects INR30-35/kg for the current quarter.
Raw material (PTA/MEG chips) moved sharply in March-April; management said it rose about 40% in April, passed through by value-add, and is now about INR100/kg of chips.
US reciprocal tariffs were struck down by the US Supreme Court; a 10% global tariff is now in place and is under legal challenge.
DGTR anti-dumping duties on Chinese and other BOPET imports recommended; Ministry of Finance notification still pending.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~15.5% adjusted EBITDA margin sustainable, and what is steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would likely stay near 15% depending on market conditions and will be far better than the last 12-15 months average; BOPET margin support expected for 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ELITe contribution and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: No P&L impact in FY27. Operations expected by end CY28 (later stated as Q4 CY28 to Q1 CY29), so major benefit from FY30; first phase about 70,000 tonnes, close to USD150 million revenue at full utilisation with 40-45% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Specialty Polymers margins and revenue soften in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality, lower demand for one key specialty product (still under assessment, not quantified), and mix shift toward lower-margin VAP products. Management says FY26 volume and value grew about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Debt reduction plan and FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Total debt about INR730-732 crore (long-term about INR380 crore). FY27 repayments about INR85 crore; capex about INR70 crore; borrowings to be kept below INR40 crore, implying INR45 crore reduction.

qa_highlights.question: How is euro-loan FX exposure being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Euro moved from about INR84 at loan sanction to about INR112 now, with about INR24 appreciation in 12-15 months. Management will partly offset via exports and take hedges opportunistically; Euribor 2.2%, with 75 bps markup, keeps cost of debt at Ester Filmtech under 7% in rupee terms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost base is crude-linked and does feedstock hit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material is a pass-through and value-add adjusts with supply-demand, so feedstock does not erode margins; VA is driven mainly by operating rates.

risks_watch: Specialty Polymers: unresolved demand loss for one marquee product; concentration risk on few products and customers acknowledged by management.
Currency: euro-denominated term loans with large MTM losses (INR37.4 crore FY26 consolidated); hedging still opportunistic.
ELITe project timing has already slipped (land acquisition pending); project depends on land and EU ESPR demand by end CY28.
Anti-dumping duties still need Ministry of Finance notification; Chinese pricing and US tariff litigation remain open.
Ester Filmtech state subsidy of INR9.57 crore approved but not yet received; upside if collected, not in P&L.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the BOPET cycle turn and FY27 outlook, but evasive on the Specialty Polymers demand issue, declining to quantify the product impact or commit to segment targets beyond 'confident'. Timelines for ELITe were acknowledged as slipping.
